introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. English Language 3 (0730), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2026. Paper 3: Section A - Summary Writing; Section B - Text Reconstruction; Section C - Editing. Duration: two hours fifteen minutes.**

ALL THE QUESTIONS ARE COMPULSORY. THEY CARRY EQUAL MARKS.

Read all instructions on BOTH the question paper and the answer booklet very carefully. Failure to obey these instructions or to number your work as on the question paper will cause you to lose marks.

Any unusual mark, sign or unnecessary disclosure of your identity will be considered as an attempt to cheat and will earn you a penalty.

In SUMMARY WRITING, use mainly your own words. Indiscriminate copying of portions of the passage as your answer will earn you no marks.

In EDITING errors created by candidates will be sanctioned.

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.
incertitudes: Page de garde : « Duration: Two Hours Fifteen Minutes » (soit 2h15), « ALL THE QUESTIONS ARE COMPULSORY. THEY CARRY EQUAL MARKS ». Aucune règle de choix : `regles_choix` est vide dans les 3 fichiers, car les trois sections sont obligatoires. Rappel imprimé : « In SUMMARY WRITING, use mainly your own words » et « In EDITING errors created by candidates will be sanctioned ».

Points : chaque section est imprimée « (15 marks) », soit 45 au total ; aucun écart constaté. Aucun corrigé officiel ni barème détaillé n'est imprimé : les corrigés sont des réponses modèles rédigées pour ce lot et la répartition interne des 15 points de chaque question est une hypothèse de correction.

Editing : le sujet ne dit pas combien de fautes il contient ; le corrigé en relève 16 (15 de langue, 1 de structure), comptées par script. La liste est celle qu'un correcteur attentif relèverait ; ce n'est pas un barème imprimé (inexistant). La faute « growing up » (devenu « living ») et le paragraphage sont des corrections défendables mais moins certaines que les autres.

Points laissés tels quels car acceptables : « my parents said I cried » (discours rapporté sans recul de temps), « in the Bimbia Camp » (article avant un nom de lieu, tournure possible), « left him to find help », « Later as an adult, » (virgule d'incise facultative). Le texte original est recopié tel qu'imprimé, y compris « It's really doing regret » (double espace sur le scan, non conservé).

La consigne imprimée demande de recopier la version corrigée et de souligner les corrections : le corrigé donne le texte corrigé et le tableau des fautes, mais le soulignement n'est pas rendu dans le texte (non faisable de façon fiable en Markdown).

questions.enonce_markdown:
**SECTION C: EDITING (15 MARKS)**

**Read through the following text carefully. Then, identify and correct all the errors in language and structure therein. Copy the edited version and underline all the corrected errors.**

I will never forget to visit Bamenda as a child. It was so exciting to stand beside the monument. It's really doing regret not to learn to play the xylophone when I had so many opportunities to learn and practise in here. When it was time for us to go home, my parents said I cried and begged them not to live. Later as an adult, growing up in the slumps of Douala, I read a newspaper article about some school boys who got lost while they were camping in the Bimbia Camp. One of the boy fell so badly and twisted the ankle so he couldn't move. Most of them stayed with the injured boy while two the older boys left him to find help. However, this two boys didn't know where to go and, after walking round in a big cycle for a few hours, ended up back with his friends. Luckily, each boys had brought some food with him, so all of them managed to survive a rainy night outdoors in the camp. They were rescued the day after the incident.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Edited text** (corrected version; 16 faults are listed below: 15 of language and 1 of structure)

I will never forget visiting Bamenda as a child. It was so exciting to stand beside the monument. I really do regret not learning to play the xylophone when I had so many opportunities to learn and practise there. When it was time for us to go home, my parents said I cried and begged them not to leave.

Later as an adult, living in the slums of Douala, I read a newspaper article about some school boys who got lost while they were camping in the Bimbia Camp. One of the boys fell so badly that he twisted his ankle and couldn't move. Most of them stayed with the injured boy while two of the older boys left him to find help. However, these two boys didn't know where to go and, after walking round in a big circle for a few hours, ended up back with their friends. Luckily, each boy had brought some food with him, so all of them managed to survive a rainy night outdoors in the camp. They were rescued the day after the incident.

**Fault-by-fault correction**

| No. | Type | Original | Correction | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Language | forget to visit | forget visiting | "Forget" + -ing refers to remembering a past event (visiting Bamenda as a child); "forget to + infinitive" means to fail to do something. |
| 2 | Language | It's really doing regret | I really do regret | "It's really doing regret" is not English; the emphatic present is "I really do regret" (subject + do + base verb). |
| 3 | Language | not to learn | not learning | "Regret" followed by -ing expresses sorrow about a past action; the negative goes before the gerund. |
| 4 | Language | practise in here | practise there | The place is in the past (Bamenda), so the distant adverb "there" is needed; "in here" is wrong in meaning and form. |
| 5 | Language | not to live | not to leave | Confusable words: "live" (reside) and "leave" (go away from); the child begged his parents not to go away. |
| 6 | Language | slumps | slums | Spelling and word choice: "slums" are poor, overcrowded districts; "slump" is a sudden fall. |
| 7 | Language | growing up | living | A person cannot "grow up" as an adult: the participle must say where the adult lived when he read the article ("having grown up" is also accepted). |
| 8 | Language | One of the boy | One of the boys | After "one of the" the noun is plural. |
| 9 | Language | twisted the ankle | twisted his ankle | A part of the body takes the possessive adjective, not the article, when the owner is clear. |
| 10 | Language | fell so badly and twisted ... so he couldn't move | fell so badly that he twisted his ankle and couldn't move | Result clause: "so + adverb + that + clause"; the second action is joined by "and", and "so" alone cannot introduce a result after "twisted". |
| 11 | Language | two the older boys | two of the older boys | Partitive structure: number + of + the + noun. |
| 12 | Language | this two boys | these two boys | The demonstrative agrees in number with the plural noun: this/these. |
| 13 | Language | big cycle | big circle | Confusable words: a "cycle" is a series of repeated events or a bicycle; walking round and round makes a "circle". |
| 14 | Language | with his friends | with their friends | The subject is "these two boys" (plural), so the possessive is "their". |
| 15 | Language | each boys | each boy | "Each" is followed by a singular countable noun (and "with him" agrees with it). |
| 16 | Structure | one block of text | two paragraphs | Paragraphing: the memory of the childhood visit and the later newspaper story are two ideas, so a new paragraph begins at "Later as an adult". |

**Marking grid (15 marks).** The paper prints only the total and asks the candidate to "identify and correct all the errors in language and structure", to copy the edited version and to underline the corrected errors; it also warns that errors created by candidates will be sanctioned. A candidate is rewarded for each fault correctly found and corrected, for underlining the corrections, and for presenting a clean copy, and loses marks for every new error introduced. The exact allocation of the 15 marks is not printed.

**Common mistakes**

1. Correcting only the spelling ("slumps", "cycle") and missing the grammar ("two the older boys", "this two boys", "each boys") and the structure (paragraphing).
2. Rewriting sentences in different words: editing means correcting the faults while keeping the writer's meaning and as much of the original wording as possible; creating a new error is sanctioned.
3. Correcting one half of a faulty sentence only, for example changing "so badly and twisted" without adding "that he", so that the sentence is still wrong; or forgetting to underline the corrections as the instructions demand.
